title: The technician's toolkit
description: Know the hand tools, testers and Windows diagnostic tools a computer technician uses, and what each one is for.
objectives: Name the essential hand tools and their uses.
Name the testers used for power, network and startup faults.
Choose the right Windows tool to investigate a problem.
tools: A technician's toolkit, if available, to identify each item

safety.text: Use the right size screwdriver. A worn or wrong-size bit strips screw heads and can slip onto the motherboard.
Do not use magnetised screwdrivers near hard drives or floppy media, and never leave loose screws inside a case.

steps.title: Hand tools
steps.body:
- **Phillips #2 screwdriver:** fits most PC screws; a **#1** or **#0** for laptops and M.2 screws.
- **Anti-static wrist strap and mat:** protect components from ESD.
- **Parts tray:** keeps screws separate and sorted.
- **Plastic spudger / pry tool:** opens laptop cases and clips without scratching.
- **Tweezers and a flashlight:** retrieve dropped screws, see into dark corners.
- **Cable ties or Velcro straps:** tidy cables for airflow.

steps.title: Testers
steps.body:
- **Multimeter:** measures voltage, resistance and continuity.
- **PSU tester:** plugs into the power supply's connectors and shows each voltage, safely.
- **POST card / debug display:** shows a code telling you where startup stopped (many boards have built-in debug LEDs instead).
- **Network cable tester:** checks each wire of a cable.
- **Loopback plug:** tests a network port by sending its signal back to itself.
- **Crimper and stripper:** make network cables.

steps.title: Supplies
steps.body:
- **Thermal paste** for reinstalling coolers
- **Isopropyl alcohol** (90%+) and lint-free cloths
- **Compressed air** for dust
- **Bootable USB drives:** a Windows installer and a diagnostics or antivirus rescue tool

steps.title: Windows diagnostic tools
steps.body:
- **Task Manager** (Ctrl+Shift+Esc): CPU, memory, disk and network use; startup programs.
- **Device Manager**: hardware and drivers; yellow icons mean a problem.
- **Event Viewer**: error logs, useful for crashes and failed services.
- **Reliability Monitor**: a timeline of crashes and changes.
- **Windows Memory Diagnostic** (`mdsched.exe`): tests RAM.
- **Command Prompt tools**: `ipconfig`, `ping`, `sfc`, `chkdsk`.
- **VocaTechX**: Network Center, Printer & Devices and the AI Troubleshooter bring many checks together.

steps.title: Match the tool to the job
steps.body:
Before you open a case, decide what you need to learn and pick the tool that tells you:

- Suspect power → PSU tester or multimeter
- Suspect RAM → Memory Diagnostic, or reseat and test one module at a time
- Suspect a cable → cable tester
- A crash → Event Viewer and Reliability Monitor
- Slow computer → Task Manager

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a flat screwdriver or a worn bit on Phillips screws.
commonMistakes.why: It slips and strips the screw head, and can scratch the board.
commonMistakes.fix: Use the correct size Phillips bit and press firmly.

commonMistakes.why: Screws differ in length and thread; a wrong one can damage the part.
commonMistakes.fix: Use a parts tray and keep screws with the part they came from.

commonMistakes.why: Replacing parts at random wastes time and money.
commonMistakes.fix: Use the tester or tool that confirms the cause first.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which tool shows where startup stops?
knowledgeChecks.answer: A POST card / debug display (or the motherboard's debug LEDs).
